transcript:
Date: 2026-03-14 | 14:30 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Park (HyperscaleGPU), Arjun Patel (Hyperscale SA), Noah Kim (Hyperscale Sales)

Summary: quick partner intro, surface technical constraints for running Redwood Dedicated on Hyperscale’s GPU fleet, and outline pilot/benchmark. Deck/benchmarks to be shared.

[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, um this is Maya from Redwood, i have Diego the solutions engineer with me. we wanted to kick off with quick intros and then get into your fleet and what partnership motions you guys are thinking about.
[00:23] Lena Park (HyperscaleGPU): thanks Maya, yeah so i'm lena, i run partnerships at hyperscale, with me are arjun who's our solutions architect and noah who owns go-to-market. excited to learn more about Redwood's offerings.
[00:45] Diego Ramos (Redwood SE): hey all, quick note - we typically talk about hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity and private deployments, depending on scale and customer needs. today maybe focussed on dedicated / partner hosting on your fleet.
[01:12] Arjun Patel (Hyperscale SA): yup we're primarily interested in how Redwood Dedicated would map onto our existing fleet; we run a mix of A100 and H100 nodes, and some Ampere instances. curious about compatibility and perf.
[01:40] Maya Chen: great, that's common. Redwood's runtime supports a variety of architectures; we pick kernels based on model arch and sequence profiles. we do quantization-friendly paths too, so the same model can run in different precisions.
[02:05] Noah Kim (Hyperscale Sales): commercial first question - are you open to a reseller / revenue share with partners who provide infra?
[02:23] Maya Chen: absolutely open, we've done reseller and referral models; details depend on committed capacity and support levels. we can share a partner deck after the call.
[02:45] Lena: technical question - network, how do you handle VPC peering and private control plane traffic for Redwood Private? we have strict peering requirements and egress constraints.
[03:08] Diego: for Redwood Private we can do a customer-controlled control plane with private endpoints, VPC peering, and optional on-prem packages. we also support direct peering and strictly restricted egress; typically we integrate with customer KMS for key management.
[03:35] Arjun: good. SOC 2 is important for our enterprise customers, and they ask about audit logs and SSO. what's your posture there?
[03:52] Maya: we are SOC 2 compliant, have audit logs, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and RBAC for tenant controls. we also support KMS/HSM integrations for key material. i'll attach the security one-pager.
[04:12] Noah: are there cases where customers want on-prem and you support that?
[04:20] Diego: yes, we have Redwood Private with an on-prem option; in those cases the control plane can be customer-managed. people sometimes use that for regulated workloads.
[04:38] Arjun: back to performance - how do you approach latency vs cost, especially for high-throughput inferencing?
[04:52] Diego: we have a smart routing layer that can send requests to cheaper model variants or fallback to hosted in spikes; we do continuous batching, prefix/KV caching, and model quantization profiles to balance latency and cost. it's a tradeoff: you can pin low-latency SLOs with dedicated capacity or favor cost with burst-to-hosted.
[05:20] Lena: do you support model offloading for KV cache or externalized caches?
[05:30] Diego: we typically keep KV cache local to the GPU runtime to avoid network penalty, but for very large contexts we have strategies to shard or externalize. there are tradeoffs.
[05:50] Maya: can i ask about your fleet size and target customers for this partnership? are you focusing on introducing Redwood to cloud customers or building a white-label offering?
[06:05] Lena: we have both - we want to provide managed inference for AI-native customers and also host platform partners who want to resell. initially we want to run a few pilots with joint customers.
[06:22] Arjun: hardware detail - we have H100 and GA100 across regions us-east1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1. any known issues with these variants?
[06:40] Diego: H100 is fine, we have optimized kernels for it; the main consideration is CUDA/driver matrix and container images. we'll need to verify the exact driver release you're on. quantization for H100 vs A100 sometimes differs.
[07:00] Noah: benchmark question - what metrics should we run in a pilot? throughput, p99 latency, cost per token?
[07:14] Maya: yes, throughput, 50/95/99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per token. also evaluate model-quality regressions if you quantize. we usually run a small subset of prompts and an eval harness.
[07:32] Diego: to add, include a tail-latency test with typical prompt distributions and some long-sequence tests to exercise KV cache.
[07:52] Arjun: security detail - for KMS do you require a particular provider? we prefer customers using AWS KMS or GCP KMS but have HSM in some partners.
[08:05] Maya: we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and can integrate with external HSMs in private deployments. we'll need to check key policy configs.
[08:20] Lena: thinking about the integration work, who's responsible for orchestration and deployment automation on your end?
[08:31] Diego: our SEs typically provide IaC templates and Helm charts for private/dedicated deployment; for partner-hosted solutions we collaborate on deployment runbooks. there is some ops work on your side for capacity ops.
[08:52] Noah: do you have any hard SLA commitments for Dedicated?
[09:00] Maya: for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets as part of reserved capacity contracts. we'll share the SLA terms in the partner packet.
[09:12] Arjun: any dependencies on specific kubernetes versions or driver versions?
[09:20] Diego: yes, we have tested matrices; we generally target k8s 1.26+ and CUDA drivers with specific minor versions. i'll capture the exact matrix in the doc.
[09:40] Lena: what about billing integration, do you send invoices to the partner or to end customers?
[09:50] Maya: both models are possible - you can resell and bill the end customer, or we can invoice through the partner. commercial terms depend on partner tier.
[10:05] Arjun: case study ask - do you have any references of running on third-party fleets?
[10:14] Maya: yes, we've run pilots with a few cloud partners and hyperscalers; i'll anonymize and share short case studies.
[10:28] Diego: technical add - for very large models we recommend sharded execution and model parallel strategies; Redwood runtime manages kernel selection and memory planning.
[10:45] Lena: excellent. one of our enterprise customers requires that the control plane never leaves their VPC, possible?
[10:56] Maya: yes that's exactly a Private deployment use case; we can deploy a control plane in your VPC or provide a customer-managed control plane. needs infra deep dive.
[11:12] Arjun: for the pilot, suggest we pick a mid-sized model like 7B to 13B and a standard RLHF chat flow, that will stress both KV cache and latency.
[11:28] Diego: agreed. 7B/13B is a good starting point — less driver hurdles and easier to benchmark.
[11:46] Maya: ok next steps, we'll send the partner deck and security one-pager; Diego will draft a benchmark plan and Arjun will share fleet spec.
[12:03] Noah: timeline - if we can get docs this week, we can line up the infra deep-dive next week.
[12:12] Lena: sounds good.
[12:20] Maya: any other questions?
[12:24] Arjun: one more - latency SLOs, do you offer built-in tracing / per-token cost visibility?
[12:34] Diego: yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. that helps for cost allocation across tenants.
[12:50] Maya: cool. we'll also attach benchmark spreadsheets with suggested tests.
[13:05] Lena: could you share the contact for SOC/compliance? we often have a security review process.
[13:14] Maya: i'll include our security contact in the email and send SOC 2 summary and relevant docs.
[13:25] Arjun: noted.
[13:34] Noah: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[13:38] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the items discussed.

[23:00] -- (call continues with more detailed Q&A; timestamps below are approximate as transcription system inserts periodic time markers)
[23:15] Diego: to be explicit on pilot metrics: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, mem usage, and cost per 1M tokens is what we track.
[29:10] Arjun: driver version on our H100s is 535. something, we'll confirm exact minor.
[35:05] Diego: okay we'll test against that driver in our lab; sometimes micro-ops differ and we want to avoid kernel fallsbacks.
[41:20] Lena: also want to know what parts of the stack we can co-brand or white-label.
[44:05] Maya: we have white-labeling options for Private deployments and partner consoles; we'll outline that in the partner packet.
[47:30] Arjun: any blockers from our side to start a pilot?
[47:40] Maya: just share fleet specs, region list, and a sample account we can use to kick off the bench.
[48:05] Noah: ok we'll circulate that.
[48:20] Maya: thanks everyone, talk soon.
